display_name: Credits for residents of the Area and for foreign workers: Income Tax Ordinance ss 48 and 48A, the Area order of 5755-1995 and the foreign worker Regulations of 5775-2014

language.note: English identifiers (@lang en); the Hebrew of every provision is quoted in `-- src:TAG:N |` comments generated mechanically from the deposited sources by tools/srcquote.py and checked line by line by tools/hebcheck.py (run by check.sh).

scope: Encoded: ITO s 48 and the Income Tax (Credits for Residents of the Area) Order 5755-1995 (ss 34, 36, 37 for a resident of the Area who is not an Israeli citizen, with s 3A(a)'s three terms); ITO s 48A and the Income Tax (Credits for a Foreign Worker) Regulations 5775-2014 (regs 1 to 4: a foreign worker, a legal one, a caring-sector one; the points under ss 34, 36, 36A; the monthly fraction; the disapplication of the rest of Chapter Three), with the Foreign Workers Law 5751-1991 s 1 definition of a foreign worker; a router for which instrument reaches a taxpayer; the combined credit points and the NIS amount before set-off. Taken as inputs: the s 1 residence test, residence in the Area, the Entry into Israel Law visa facts, the value of a credit point. Not encoded: ss 34, 36, 36A, 37 themselves (IL-01, IL-08), s 66 (IL-02), s 3A(f) (IL-01), s 33A/120B (IL-01, IL-03). Seven forks (F1, F2, F4 carried from IL-01; FW1, FW2, FW3, OV) are switches, by default declining by name (Meng's ruling SHRUG of 2026-10-08).

years_answered.Area order: tax years 2017 onwards; s 37 from 2023; 1995 to 2016 refused (s 3A text and the Order's start within 1995); before 1995 refused (no earlier order deposited)
years_answered.foreign worker Regulations: tax years 2019 onwards; 2015 to 2018 refused (the Regulations as made and as first amended are not deposited); 2002 to 2014 fork FW2 (default refused); before 2002 s 48A did not exist

inputs.published_figures: none carried; the tests use NIS 2,904 per credit point as an illustrative input, the figure row IL-01 carries from the Israel Tax Authority for 2025 (not law)

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this encoding against the source, and no independent test pass has been run yet. Every expected value in the tests was worked by hand from the Hebrew before the code was run.

forks.F1: s 36A has no residence limb: does a woman who is not an Israeli resident get its half point? Carried from IL-01. A: no condition; B: only an Israeli resident; default declined.
forks.F2: s 36's quarter point and income from personal exertion. Carried from IL-01. Default declined where it decides.
forks.F4: A resident of the Area for only part of the tax year (ss 34, 36 under the Order). Carried from IL-01. A: one status; B: apportioned by months as s 41(1); default declined where they differ.
forks.FW1: Do the cited sections' residence conditions still bind a foreign worker who is not an Israeli resident, under reg 3? A: no; B: yes. Default declined where they differ.
forks.FW2: Tax years 2002 to 2014: did an instrument under s 48A apply before the Regulations (reg 4: 2015)? A: none; default declined.
forks.FW3: Reg 3(d) disapplies 'the provisions of Chapter Three' but s 48A's power speaks of credits: does it reach the deductions of ss 47 and 47A? A: credits only; B: the whole chapter; default declined.
forks.OV: A foreign worker who is also a resident of the Area who is not an Israeli citizen is reached by both instruments: which prevails? A: the Regulations; B: the Order; default declined.
